q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) AS COUNT FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS ) AS FOO WHERE COUNT >= 5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) AS COUNT FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS ) AS FOO WHERE COUNT >= 5
explanation: Q1 groups by CLASS and checks if the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class is >= 5. Q2 groups by CLASS, counts the distinct students in each class, and then checks if this count is >= 5. The difference lies in the COUNT function used: Q1 uses COUNT(*), while Q2 uses COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT). This means Q1 considers all rows (students) in a class, whereas Q2 considers only unique students.
counterexample_dsp: A class with 5 students where 2 students are enrolled twice. Q1 will count all 7 rows, while Q2 will count only 5 unique students.
